prompts.title: Form Pulse: Croacia vs España
prompts.prompt: Title: 'Form Pulse: Croacia vs España'. 9:16 vertical composition on GoatLab charcoal #101412, warm white #edf0e6 type, lime #c5ed74 emphasis and slate #8ca6bf secondary. Reserve the lower quarter for permanent yellow subtitles. Editorial variant first: kinetic typography and rhythmic emphasis, no statistical axes, no sample claims and no invented match events. Spanish team labels Croacia and España sit as opposing vertical columns. Spanish category words 'Victorias', 'Empates', 'Derrotas' enter as bold staccato blocks, each word snapped by a beat, with lime underline sweeps and slate ghost echoes. Rhythmic emphasis increases as the narration names results; empty spaces pulse when a word is absent. Camera drifts slowly upward and then tilts between columns. Transition: hard whip-pan from Croacia to España, then soft dissolve on a held split frame. Exit on a clean two-column lock-up, subtitles still protected. Statistical variant: grouped count bars for recent form, one cluster per team, shared zero baseline, x-axis Spanish labels 'Victorias', 'Empates', 'Derrotas', y-axis unit 'partidos'. Croacia bars use {{home.wins}}, {{home.draws}}, {{home.losses}}; España bars use {{away.wins}}, {{away.draws}}, {{away.losses}}. Sample annotation uses {{home.n}} and {{away.n}}, with a source/sample note from Bzzoiro kept small but legible. If resolved sample sizes differ, place an honest 'muestras desiguales' flag above the smaller cluster and never normalise into rates. Entry animation: baseline draws first, then bars grow in staggered order, team labels fading in before counts. Main comparison: paired clusters separated by a central gutter, common scale visible in the y-axis. Emphasis: lime glow on the leading bar per category, slate for the trailing bar. Camera: subtle lateral drift, no zoom beyond frame. Transition: slide to the next category cluster or crossfade to the editorial close. Exit: bars settle, source annotation remains, lower quarter free for Spanish subtitles. Duration adapts to spoken words across approximately 6–10 seconds.
